description.narrative: The overall goal of the project is to contribute to the efforts of ensuring that citizens of Isiolo and Marsabit counties benefit from inclusive and participatory county governance development processes.

The overall goal of the project is to contribute to the efforts of ensuring that citizens of Isiolo and Marsabit counties benefit from inclusive and participatory county governance development processes.

The projects interventions will be focused on the North Frontier counties of Isiolo and Marsabit. Despite the goodwill of the Constitution to reduce the levels of marginalisation across Kenya, the residents of Isiolo and Marsabit counties still live on the periphery of society, systemically excluded from the mainstream social, political, economic, and cultural development. They experience recurrent challenges of abject poverty, condensed economic activities limited to pastoralism, political under-representation, and limited inclusion and public participation in the counties development agenda. Both counties are Arid and Semi-Arid Land (ASAL) and are negatively affected by climate change, which is often a trigger of conflict. The latter occurs specifically among pastoralists communities belonging to different ethnic groups, who, because of extreme climatic events, are forced to look for pasture and other natural resources, often invading the boundaries of other communities and counties.
The geographical inaccessibility of many areas of especially Marsabit County but lso border areas of Isiolo county also exacerbates the marginalisation of its communities, with the majority of the State institutions unable and unwilling to penetrate these areas. Building on the 2030 Agenda for sustainable development and the principle of leaving no one behind, the project will focus its interventions in these two counties.
It is expected that at the end of the intervention, the project will contribute to the efforts of ensuring that citizens of Isiolo and Marsabit counties benefit from inclusive and participatory county governance development processes and that the county Governments of Isiolo and Marsabit, will increasingly drive transparency, and accountability actions, including on climate change and Natural resource management. In addition, the residents will be exposed to contextualised multi-door approaches to justice, including court annexed mediation (CAM) and Alternative justice systems (AJS) platforms, which will increase their chances of effectively solving their disputes in a fairer, cheaper, and more effective manner. It is also envisaged that there will be improved ability of women, especially young women, in Isiolo and Marsabit counties to access public information and effectively participate in county-level governance processes as well as an improved capacity of the county Governments of Isiolo and Marsabit to implement gender-responsive county-level climate change and NRM Actions for inclusive climate resilience development.

IDLO continued to implement activities to improve the County Governments of Isiolo and Marsabits ability to drive transparency and accountability actions on climate change and NRM processes by facilitating efficient commercial justice systems that respond to key indicators of an improved business climate. The first half of the year was committed to inception interventions, including undertaking (i) a security risk assessment, which was considered necessary given the security risks identified in Isiolo and Marsabit Counties that could negatively affect project implementation; and (ii) a baseline assessment in both Counties, which presented a comprehensive and in-depth analysis of the broader context regarding transparency and accountability initiatives, climate change, and NRM efforts.
IDLO also supported initiatives to expand the multi-door approach to justice by supporting initiatives towards the roll-out of Court Annexed Mediation (CAM) and coordinated the establishment of Alternative Justice System (AJS) centres. IDLO also focused on support for inclusive and informed public participation in developing and implementing climate change and NRM actions through community engagements with the county governments.
Some of the successes of the project in 2023 and 2024 were:
Outcome 1 Establishment of a Court AJS in Isiolo and Marsabit counties: IDLO engaged a consultant to support the National Steering Committee on Implementation of the Alternative Justice Policy (NaSCI-AJS) in the development of Isiolo and Marsabit County Action Plans (CAPs). The CAPs set the stage for establishing accessible and user-friendly AJS suites as a framework for administering the Court Annexed AJS programme. These refer to AJS processes used to resolve disputes outside the court by the Council of Elders under the guidance and partial involvement of the court. The suites are offices the Judiciary allocates to resolve cases through the AJS programme.
In 2024, IDLO provided expert and convening support for the training of 65 judicial officers (F: 29; M: 36) from Marsabit and Isiolo Law Courts in Meru. The training sessions were conducted from 29 April to 2 May 2024 in Marsabit and from 15 to 17 May 2024 in Isiolo. The training sessions aimed at enhancing the capacity of judicial officers on AJS, CAM, and climate change. As a result of the training, the pre- and post-training assessments demonstrated an average 32-percentage point increase in participants knowledge on AJS, CAM, and climate change.
In September 2024, Sweden participated in the launch of the AJS Suits in Isiolo. The occassion was graced by the Chief Justice. The launch of the AJS suits in Marsabit is planned for November 2024.
Establishment of Court Annexed Mediation Registries: IDLO supported the Judiciarys CAM Secretariat and the Mediation Accreditation Committee (MAC) to roll out CAM and expand pathways/doors for justice to vulnerable groups in both Isiolo and Marsabit courts. IDLO delivered professional certified training on mediation for qualified citizens as per the selection criteria prescribed by the MAC, and established a pool of 80 mediators (F: 31; M: 49). This will enhance opportunities for a successful mediation process. IDLO also delivered contextualized mediation training for judges, magistrates, registrars, and clerks on the operational framework and effective administration of CAM.
Furthermore, in 2024 IDLO supported the roll-out of CAM in Isiolo and Marsabit Law Courts to provide alternative justice solutions. During the roll-out, the CAM Secretariat inducted the registry staff, and judicial officers on the CAM operational frameworks, mediation screening processes and referral of matters, provision of spaces for mediation sessions, management and payment of mediators, and adoption of settlement agreements from mediation processes. Since the engagement of mediation clerks in April 2024, the accredited mediators, trained by IDLO in 2023, have handled 25 cases. Out of these, nine (9) cases have been fully concluded, with 16 ongoing. The majority of the cases handled include land disputes, child custody and maintenance, succession as well as civil cases such as debt. This initiative aims to enhance the capacity of the courts to resolve cases expeditiously
Outcome 2
Launch of the Marsabit County Climate Change Action Plan (MCCCAP): IDLO supported the County Government of Marsabit to review and integrate gender-responsive action plans into the MCCCAP. The MCCCAP is a key milestone towards addressing the Countys vulnerability to climate change and identifies specific investment areas to build resilience to climate change in the County. The MCCCAP was launched on 28 November 2023. In 2024, IDLO provided expert support to the Kenya Judiciary Academy (KJA) to facilitate the development of the Climate Change and Environmental Law training curriculum. The training curriculum aims to provide judicial officers with the relevant knowledge and skills to resolve climate change justice and environmental rights matters effectively. The training curriculum is currently undergoing final validation by the KJA while pending incorporation into the KJA e-learning platform.
Facilitating access to information to increase participation of virtually impaired persons: IDLO supported the Commission on Administration of Justice (CAJ) in translating the Simplified Booklet on the Access to Information Act and Regulations, 2016 (ATI Act) into Braille. Their translation into Braille promotes a more inclusive opportunity to enhance access to relevant information on access to justice and facilitates effective participation in the development of climate change action plans
Delivery of Training of Trainers (TOTs) on Access to Information: IDLO facilitated the CAJ to carry out a five-day TOT session on the ATI Act for 30 (F: 12; M: 18) county government officers in Isiolo and Marsabit Counties. The TOT sought to facilitate effective knowledge transfer on implementing the ATI Act and create effective communication structures between the county government and community members on climate change and natural resource management. The TOTs will form part of the established database by the CAJ for trainers on the administration of the ATI Act. The county government officers are now informed on how to responsibly provide access to public information to members of the public on request. They will more easily identify the information required for effective public participation in county governance processes.
Outcome 3.
Furthermore in 2024, IDLO supported the establishment of the ELC CUC in Isiolo. The ELC CUC provides a platform to bring together court actors and users to enhance public participation and stakeholder engagement in matters related to environment and land. It also promotes effective justice sector partnerships for a coordinated, efficient, effective and consultative approach to the administration of justice in the court. The platform aims to address land, environmental and climate justice needs of justice seekers within Isiolo County.
IDLO supported the establishment of the Marsabit GCCC through convening and expert support. The Marsabit GCCC, comprising representatives from the Ward Planning Committee (WPC), aims to address the intersection of gender and climate change at the ward level. Its mandate, derived from the WPC's role, includes consulting with the community on inclusive and gender-responsive climate finance activities, facilitating inclusive public participation with vulnerable groups, receiving gender-responsive project proposals from the community, and monitoring the implementation of projects to ensure the integration of gender equality and inclusion of the most vulnerable groups in county climate actions.
IDLO in partnership with the Isiolo and Marsabit County Governments developed a report on the disproportionate impacts of climate change and NRM on women and girls in the two (2) Counties. The report provides a deeper understanding of the disproportionate impacts of climate change on women and girls including on food security, education, and access to resources in both counties; and proposes response measures to mitigate the impact. The mitigation measures against climate impact proposed include involvement of women in decision-making, enhancement of womens capacity in the climate change discourse, and ensuring that there are gender-sensitive legal and institutional frameworks at the county level.
From 21-23 February 2024, IDLO offered expert and convening support to the Marsabit County government to train members of the Marsabit County Climate Change Unit and executive officers on the intersection between climate change and gender towards more equitable and sustainable solutions to climate change. In attendance were 18 (F: 5; M: 13) participants drawn from various departments within the County government of Marsabit, which include Environment, Gender, Water and Sanitation, Economics and Planning, Disaster Management, and Agriculture. The pre- and post-training assessment revealed that on average, participants demonstrated a 30- percentage point increase in knowledge on climate change and NRM.
